::: {.lede}
Most of what I make is not a paper. Devices, tasks and analysis pipelines are
research output too, and they are easier to check than a methods section.
:::

## Force-matching device {.k-head}

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
Hardware &middot; for the thesis protocol &middot; [calibrating]{.status .pending}
:::
:::

A two-channel force transducer rig for the force-matching task, designed and
machined in-house with my brother Anıl Bekdemir, a mechanical engineer, who
worked on it unpaid. The acquisition software is mine. Built because
commercial equivalents cost more than the grant and could not be modified.

Mechanically complete; calibration is still in progress. The calibration data
and build notes will be published with it.

## Beads task {.k-head}

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
PsychoPy &middot; [to publish]{.status}
:::
:::

Probabilistic reasoning task with trial-level logging, written for modelling

## HGF analysis pipeline {.k-head}

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
Python / TAPAS &middot; [to publish]{.status}
:::
:::

Model fitting, parameter and model recovery, and Bayesian model selection,
with the recovery simulations that ran before any participant was seen.

## GÖRÜNGÜ {.k-head}

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
Python &middot; OpenCV &middot; MIT &middot; [public]{.status .done}
:::
:::

Optical mark recognition and automatic scoring for paper psychiatric
assessment forms, so that scale batteries stop being typed in by hand.
Interactive template design, per-form threshold tuning, automatic alignment of
photographed sheets, and CSV export.
[Repository](https://github.com/frknbkdmr/gorungu).
